title: PulsePoint clinical embeddings optimization impact study
content:
Purpose and audience:
This working spreadsheet + analysis summarizes the before/after cost and performance impact of Redwood Optimize recommendations for PulsePoint Health (clinical search + similarity embeddings). Primary audience: solutions engineering, customer success, and PulsePoint procurement.

Status and context:
- Customer: PulsePoint Health (medtech search for clinical notes and patient matching).
- Scope: Embedding generation (batch and on-demand), storage and serving costs, and inference model substitutions for generation-based features used in triage pipeline.
- Engagement: 6-week pilot with telemetry from Sept–Oct 2025. This doc is a draft impact study derived from raw billing + telemetry and the Optimize recommendations we applied in week 4.
- Note: numbers are modeled with conservative assumptions and include a sensitivity analysis for query volume +/-25%.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline monthly cost (PulsePoint reported): $68,400 (embedding generation + tiny hosted rerank/generation usage).
- Post-optimize projected cost (recommended changes applied): $38,900/mo — estimated 43% reduction in monthly inference spend.
- Primary drivers: model swap to quantized 8-bit embedding model for batch jobs (-28%), aggressive batching of on-demand embedding requests (-7%), prefix KV cache for triage reranks (-5%), and embedding delta deduplication & TTL pruning (-3%).
- Risks: slight accuracy drift on clinical synonyms interactions with aggressive quantization; requires 1% sample QA and rollback window.

Summary table (monthly):

| Category                         | Baseline ($) | After Optimize ($) | Delta ($) | Notes |
|----------------------------------|--------------:|-------------------:|----------:|-------|
| Embedding generation (batch)     | 30,200       | 21,400             | -8,800    | Batch jobs moved to q8hw variant + larger minibatches (x2 tokens/batch) |
| Embedding generation (on-demand) | 18,900       | 13,300             | -5,600    | Batching middleware + 200ms coalescing + cache for repeated requests |
| Serving/embedding storage ops    | 6,100        | 5,200              | -900      | TTL pruning and dedupe drop ~12% of store ops |
| Reranker/generation             | 11,200       | 2,100              | -9,100    | Move from large-gen model to targeted lightweight rerank + fallback |
| Network & infra overhead         | 2,000        | 2,900              | +900      | Slight increase due to caching infra + read replicas |
| TOTAL                            | 68,400       | 38,900             | -29,500   | 43% total savings

Assumptions and measurement basis:
- Billing window used: 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-15 telemetry export (raw token/embedding counts).
- Pricing model used: Redwood hosted per-embedding unit USD rates (baseline) and recommended quantized model pricing (post-Optimize), plus typical token-rate for generation calls.
- Workload shapes: 70% batch offline embedding refreshes (nightly), 30% on-demand API calls. Latency SLO for on-demand: 250ms p50, 600ms p99.
- Accuracy guardrail: semantic similarity AUC on annotated clinical testset (N=3,000 pairs). Baseline AUC: 0.88. Post-change expected AUC range: 0.86–0.88. We require A/B validation with N=2,000 live queries to confirm no more than 0.02 AUC drop.

Recommendations applied (details):
1) Quantized model for batch embedding generation (q8hw variant):
   - Rationale: Batch jobs can tolerate tiny accuracy tradeoffs for large unit-cost improvements.
   - Implementation: swap nightly job model, add fallback to full float model for 0.5% sample checks.
   - Expected: ~28% cost reduction for batch embedding compute.

2) On-demand batching middleware + 200–300ms coalescing window:
   - Rationale: High fraction of identical/near-identical requests during peak hours due to dashboard refreshes.
   - Implementation: lightweight in-proc batcher in API gateway; max batch size 64; per-tenant batching knob.
   - Operational note: Monitor tail latency (p99) and provide opt-out per route if SLO violated.

3) Prefix/KV caching for rerank step:
   - Rationale: Many reranks reuse prefixes (patient context) across parallel requests.
   - Implementation: short-lived KV cache on serving nodes (TTL 30s) - sensitive to privacy window for clinical data, so encrypt keys and add audit entries.

4) Deduplication + TTL pruning for embedding store:
   - Rationale: PulsePoint stored near-duplicate embeddings from repeated ingestion; removing duplicates reduces storage and read ops.
   - Implementation: weekly dedupe job + incremental TTL removal for items older than 90 days unless flagged.

5) Model routing / fallback policy:
   - Rationale: Keep primary q8 models for cost but automatically route to full-precision variants when QA checks detect drift or when query flagged as high-risk.
   - Implementation: Canary ratio 5% to high-precision model; automatic rollback if AUC drop >0.01 over 48h.

Customer-specific sensitivity analysis (monthly cost):
- Volume scenarios modeled: Base (current), +25% traffic, -25% traffic.

Base: baseline $68,400 -> optimized $38,900 (43% reduction)
+25% volume: baseline $85,500 -> optimized $48,700 (43% reduction)
-25% volume: baseline $51,300 -> optimized $29,200 (43% reduction)

(percentage savings consistent because per-unit improvements apply across volume ranges; fixed infra overhead reduces effectiveness slightly at very low volumes).

Operational playbook / rollout checklist (recommended 3-phase):
- Phase 0 (preflight): sign MOU, enable telemetry export, snapshot existing AUC and p99 latency baselines. -> Owner: SE (Kofi)
- Phase 1 (canary): enable q8 batch for nightly job + 5% canary routing for rerank; collect metrics 7 days -> Owner: Eng (Lina)
- Phase 2 (incremental ramp): enable batching middleware for on-demand with 200ms window, enable dedupe job -> Owner: Customer Success (Rae)
- Phase 3 (full): flip default routing and turn off float-nightly except for sample checks; finalize cost-share contract. -> Owner: Solutions Eng + Finance

Key monitoring signals to watch (alerts):
- AUC delta > 0.01 over 48h on live annotated set (alert to SE)
- p99 latency regression > 200ms on on-demand routes (alert to SRE)
- Canary error increase > 0.5% absolute (alert to Eng)
- Storage ops delta not matching predicted reductions (ops review)

Open questions / next steps:
- Confirm privacy/legal acceptability of 30s KV cache for PHI contexts; push to Security for sign-off.
- Agree on acceptable AUC delta and sample size for live validation.
- Determine commercial credit structure for first 3 months of ramp (Finance to propose).

Appendix A — simplified calculation excerpt (monthly):
- Inputs (from telemetry): monthly_embedding_ops_batch = 1,250,000 units; monthly_embedding_ops_on_demand = 780,000 units; avg_tokens_rerank = 1.2M tokens/month.
- Pricing: baseline embedding unit = $0.012/unit; q8 model embedding unit = $0.008/unit; generation token rate baseline = $0.00006/token; lightweight rerank token rate = $0.000015/token.

Calc snippet (batch):
 baseline_batch = 1,250,000 * $0.012 = $15,000 compute + $15,200 infra overhead = $30,200 total
 after_q8 = 1,250,000 * $0.008 = $10,000 compute + $11,400 infra overhead = $21,400 total
 savings = $8,800 (~29%)

Appendix B — recommended tickets (placeholder):
- ENG-4721: implement q8 variant in nightly pipeline (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/189)
- OPT-238: batching middleware prototype for on-demand routes
- SEC-1192: KV cache PHI review and encrypt-at-rest design

Notes / doc provenance:
- This is a working doc; numbers will be reconciled during final billing sync. For the canonical copy after sign-off, we will export a one-pager for PulsePoint and attach the detailed spreadsheet with raw telemetry.

If you want, I can export this into a lightweight one-page proposal for the customer with executive bullets and cost table only (suitable for procurement).
